I’ll start by reading the handoff document and checking the repository’s current branch/status and structure. Then I’ll map the existing end-to-end flow and integration seams before making changes on a new branch.

The handoff confirms the repo is at the post-onboarding merge point: cfo.ai, neatlogs, and Entire setup modules exist, but the first-user path still needs an integrated proof run and the integrations are mostly setup/recording adapters rather than a cohesive workflow. I’m creating a dedicated branch now, then I’ll run the existing checks to establish a baseline before tightening the flow.

The working tree is clean, but this environment mounts `.git` read-only, so a normal branch creation cannot write the ref. I’ll request the narrow repository-control permission needed to create the branch; source edits remain inside the workspace.

The baseline cannot run yet because this checkout has no installed dependencies (`vitest`/`tsc` are missing); no source changes have been made. I’m now tracing `init → doctor → plan/run → ledger/dashboard` and the three integration adapters so the implementation targets the actual end-to-end breakpoints rather than just adding setup prompts.

content.text: The baseline is largely healthy: 483 tests pass, typecheck and build pass. Two test failures are environment-related in this sandbox (one needs a local AO binary, one needs loopback binding); I’ll preserve those as validation caveats and use focused fake-based tests plus an escalated full suite later. The main product gap I’m targeting is now clear: the run can record each adapter independently, but it does not expose a single durable “integration contract” tying budget, decision traces, worker traces, code-graph evidence, verification, and PR publication together.

I found a concrete first-user bug in the handoff path: re-running `tally init` only flips integration booleans; it never invokes the guided cfo.ai/neatlogs/Entire setup, so a skipped integration can be “enabled” with no usable configuration. I’m fixing that first, including safe rollback to the local budget when cfo.ai is disabled, then I’ll harden optional telemetry and graph behavior.

I’ve isolated the main flow gap: re-running `tally init` could enable integrations without running their guided setup, while the run path also had a few reliability/accounting edge cases. I’m tightening those contracts now, then I’ll run the focused and full test suites before committing and opening the PR from the feature branch.

content.text: One accounting edge surfaced in the test review: a resumed run needs to distinguish “the saved local ledger is already reflected in cfo.ai” from “the earlier cfo.ai write failed and must be synced.” I’m making that state explicit so resumes don’t double-count successful history or silently omit fallback history.

 ### Configuration
+
+### How the integrations cooperate
+
+The integrations are deliberately complementary rather than competing sources
+of truth during one run:
+
+1. The backlog is read from GitHub or the configured file. Entire graph signals
+   are used for sizing when enabled; the graph is indexed once per run and
+   Tally falls back to repository code search if it is unavailable.
+2. The CFO agent routes each task and enforces the local safety ceiling. When
+   cfo.ai is enabled, its live monthly budget and spend are the accounting
+   authority. Tally still writes the local integer-nanos ledger and a
+   `cfoai-spend-fallback.csv`; a resumed run reconciles only the spend that is
+   missing remotely and can re-sync a prior failed fallback.
+3. neatlogs records route, ceiling, worker and verification evidence. Trace
+   export is optional telemetry: a network/export failure does not execute a
+   task twice or turn completed work into a failed run. Worker hook batches are
+   drained outside the worker sandbox and failed batches stay queued for a
+   later run.
+4. Verification, changed-file scope, checkpoint metadata and the final ledger
+   are persisted locally. A passing task is published as a branch/PR; Tally
+   does not merge it.
+
+For the first live handoff from one operator to another, use this sequence:
+
+1. Run `tally init` or re-run it to enable integrations; complete the guided
+   setup and review the proposed diff.
+2. Run `tally doctor`, then `tally run --plan --dry-run`; confirm the task count,
+   route, ceiling and budget source.
+3. Run `tally run --dry-run` and inspect the generated `run.json`, `ledger.json`
+   and dashboard before spending real worker time.
+4. Start one real labeled task with `tally run --only <task-id>`. Check the PR,
+   verification result, cfo.ai spend, neatlogs trace/worker evidence and
+   Entire checkpoint metadata.
+5. Hand over the branch, `tally.yaml`, the latest run directory and any
+   pending integration fix printed by `tally doctor`. Keep credentials outside
+   the repository; the next operator can rerun onboarding without rewriting
+   unrelated configuration.

 its own process, outside the worker sandbox. It uses the official package's
*** End Patch";
